question: Can a same-state conventional KC reconstruction source a registered stationary edge-variance proxy and conditional load shape?
assumptions: Fixed lower sheet, 14 upper heights, 16 A fixed pair roster and 1.44 eV plate
Classical local Gaussian covariance about stationary model point
Physical proxy q_e=h_B-h_A is posited, not native-derived
Independent passive height loss dI and pressure-constant beta,d,T only for illustrative pure-port slope
physical_mapping: OPEN native signed/even packet variable to physical bond heights; C is conventional mixed Hessian
target_exposure: Archive and 21.8/38.2 friction peak known; fitted beta uses conventional C; no held-out experimental trace
fitted_choices: one scalar beta fitted to conventional C for exploratory shape comparison
sources: arXiv:2308.06302 SI Table S1, source SHA adea7468f311c648a0d25abf4f5eecacd8eebe1b6fc7761ffcea7d073b2f460b
baseline: v19/v20 conventional KC-plus-plate reconstruction and v3 manuscript identifiability limit
result: Matched K/C reconstructed within 1.5e-8 relative tensor differences to archived model; bond-variance proxy nonuniform and rank-two; conditional pure-port slope 6.74813e-4 /MPa at fixed beta,d,T
next_discriminant: Independent native-to-material edge mapping, measured D(omega,P), contact response and signed held-out force/load
